summary: Solution Design Document for the app-shell redesign (round 2, amended after architecture-critic's round-1 BLOCKED verdict on finding AC-1). Constrained by tech-lead's FEAT-1 decision record (D1-D6, hard_constraints_for_solution_architect) and .claude/rules/frontend.md. No application code written at this stage per solution-architect.md's scope (SDD only) — code generation begins at stage 3.5 (Engineer/MVP). Round 2 change: app_jsx_change and routing_design were amended so the hash decision wraps the entire Header/main/Footer tree instead of nesting inside <main> — the app-shell branch now renders <AppShell/> alone, with no marketing Header/Footer mounted alongside it. All other round-1 sections (component_breakdown, supporting_modules, design_tokens, dependency_decision, propTypes_plan) are unchanged and were re-verified as still consistent with this fix.
scope_note: Stage 3 produces the design document that stages 3.1 (Architecture Critic), 3.3 (System Engineer) and 3.5 (Engineer/MVP) build from. Component code is intentionally not written here.

component_breakdown.role: Top-level internal-app container. Renders Sidebar + TopBar + a content outlet. Owns activeViewId as local useState, derived from an initialHash prop on mount so an incoming '#master-data' link pre-selects the Master Data nav item.

state.activeViewId: string — id of the entry in NAV_ITEMS currently shown in the content outlet

children_rendered: the active NAV_ITEMS entry's component (MasterDataView for id 'master-data')

component_breakdown.role: Persistent left nav. Pure presentational list of NAV_ITEMS, highlights activeId, calls onSelect(id) on click. No routing/hash knowledge — AppShell owns that.
Workspace chrome bar: current section title (derived from the active NAV_ITEMS entry's label) + UserBadge on the right. Purely presentational.

props.title: string
props.user: shape({ name: string, role: string, initials: string })

component_breakdown.role: Signed-in-user chip: initials avatar + name + role. Calls useCurrentUser() itself so any consumer can drop it in without prop drilling the mock user.

supporting_modules.role: Single explicitly-named mock export, MOCK_CURRENT_USER = { id, name, role, initials }. No token, no email persistence, no auth call — matches enterprise-architect-pre condition 3 and tech-lead D3. Uses a fictitious placeholder identity, not any real person's data.

Returns MOCK_CURRENT_USER as-is. The single seam future real-auth work replaces — every consumer (UserBadge, and TopBar via AppShell) goes through this hook, never src/mock/currentUser.js directly, per tech-lead's risk note 3.

NAV_ITEMS registry: [{ id: 'master-data', label: 'Master Data', hash: '#master-data', component: MasterDataView }]. Single array AppShell/Sidebar both read — the extension point tech-lead flagged for a second future module (add one entry, no new nav mechanism). Also exports APP_SHELL_HASHES (hashes that mean 'render AppShell'), derived from NAV_ITEMS so App.jsx and AppShell can't drift out of sync.

routing_design.decision_point: App.jsx's existing useLocationHash remains the ONLY hash-driven decision, and it is now the OUTERMOST decision in the render tree (revised in round 2 per architecture-critic AC-1) — it decides between the entire app-shell branch and the entire marketing branch, not just the <main> content between a shared Header/Footer. hash is looked up against APP_SHELL_HASHES (from src/lib/navigation.js, currently just '#master-data'): match -> <AppShell initialHash={hash} /> alone (no Header/Footer); no match -> <Header/><main>Hero/ServicesSection/DeliveryCenters</main><Footer/>, unchanged from today.
routing_design.internal_navigation: Inside AppShell, clicking a Sidebar item calls setActiveViewId(id) — plain useState, NOT a hash change. This is a deliberate, tech-lead-mandated trade-off: no second router layer. Consequence: the browser back button and deep-linking only work for the entry hash (e.g. '#master-data'), not for whichever internal view is currently selected. Documented here so stage 3.1 (Architecture Critic) evaluates it as an accepted trade-off, not an oversight.
routing_design.hash_collision_resolution: '#master-data' is now consumed entirely by NAV_ITEMS/APP_SHELL_HASHES — App.jsx has exactly one place that lists internal-app hashes, so there is no second branch that could diverge from it (resolves tech-lead's flagged hash-collision risk).
routing_design.app_shell_owns_its_own_chrome: AppShell's TopBar (title + UserBadge) is the app-shell branch's equivalent of page chrome — it replaces Header/Footer entirely on app-shell hashes, it does not sit alongside them. This is the direct fix for architecture-critic finding AC-1 (round 1): the marketing Header (anchor-nav + 'Talk to Us' CTA) and marketing Footer (#about/#contact anchors) must never render while an app-shell hash is active, because they duplicate/contradict Sidebar navigation and read as public-portal chrome around an internal dashboard.

app_jsx_change.revision_reason: architecture-critic (stage 3.1) BLOCKED round 1 with Critical finding AC-1: round 1's design only swapped <main>'s children between AppShell and the marketing fragment, leaving <Header/> and <Footer/> mounted unconditionally around BOTH branches — so the new dashboard still rendered sandwiched inside the old public-portal chrome. Fixed by moving the branch decision one level up, per AC-1's required_fix, while keeping tech-lead's 'single hash-driven top-level decision point' constraint intact (the decision is still exactly one ternary on `hash`, just now wrapping Header/main/Footer instead of nesting inside <main>).
imports_removed: MasterDataView (moved to being imported only by src/lib/navigation.js)
imports_unchanged_but_now_conditional: Header — only rendered in the marketing branch
Footer — only rendered in the marketing branch

data_flow: App.jsx reads hash via useLocationHash (unchanged hook).
App.jsx passes hash to AppShell only when it's an app-shell hash.
AppShell resolves initialHash -> activeViewId via NAV_ITEMS lookup (fallback: NAV_ITEMS[0].id).
AppShell renders Sidebar(items=NAV_ITEMS, activeId=activeViewId, onSelect=setActiveViewId) and TopBar(title=<active item's label>, user=useCurrentUser()).

AppShell renders the active NAV_ITEMS entry's component in the content outlet (MasterDataView today) — MasterDataView's own internal state (tabs, table data fetching via useMasterDataTable) is untouched.

new_additive_tokens_in_src_index_css.reason: Sidebar column width — no existing token covers a fixed layout dimension.
TopBar row height, used for sticky offset math.

reused_existing_tokens: --color-bg, --color-bg-alt (panel/surface backgrounds — no new surface token needed, --color-bg-alt already serves this)
design_tokens.constraint_honored: No existing token renamed or redefined — Header/Hero/Footer/ServicesSection/DeliveryCenters/MasterDataView are unaffected.

dependency_decision.justification: frontend.md mandates PropTypes on every component; it does not currently exist in package.json anywhere in the codebase. This is a validation-only micro-library (React's own former built-in, split out at React 15), not a router, UI kit, or state-management library — it does not conflict with tech-lead's 'no new runtime dependency' constraint, which specifically named those three categories. Flagging explicitly rather than silently adding it, per CLAUDE.md's no-laziness/explicit-tradeoffs principle.
dependency_decision.action_for_next_stage: Engineer (3.5) runs `npm install prop-types` when implementing.

propTypes_plan.Sidebar: items: PropTypes.arrayOf(PropTypes.shape({ id: PropTypes.string.isRequired, label: PropTypes.string.isRequired })).isRequired, activeId: PropTypes.string.isRequired, onSelect: PropTypes.func.isRequired
propTypes_plan.TopBar: title: PropTypes.string.isRequired, user: PropTypes.shape({ name: PropTypes.string.isRequired, role: PropTypes.string.isRequired, initials: PropTypes.string.isRequired }).isRequired

out_of_scope_for_this_feature: MasterDataTable/MasterDataView internal refactor — left as-is per tech-lead D4.
Retrofitting PropTypes onto existing marketing components — per tech-lead D6.
Real authentication — mock only, per enterprise-architect-pre condition 3.
A second internal module / view-registry beyond the single Master Data entry — YAGNI per tech-lead's risk note, NAV_ITEMS array is the documented extension point when one appears.
constraints_verified_against: No new router/UI-kit/state-management dependency (prop-types is the one explicitly-justified exception, documented above).

Marketing components remain untouched and decoupled — only App.jsx's conditional branch changes, no import of AppShell into marketing components or vice versa. Header/Footer are now conditionally rendered (marketing branch only) rather than unconditionally wrapping both branches — see app_jsx_change round 2.
Signed-in-user context is a clearly-named mock behind one hook seam.

Single hash-driven top-level decision point; all further nav is React state. Round 2: this decision point is now the outermost render decision (wraps Header/main/Footer), not nested inside <main> — still exactly one ternary on `hash`.
PropTypes required on every new component (see propTypes_plan).
One component per folder, CSS Modules, camelCase classes, additive tokens only.
App-shell branch renders no marketing chrome (Header/Footer) alongside AppShell — resolves architecture-critic finding AC-1.

round1_findings_resolved.resolution: app_jsx_change and routing_design amended (see 'round': 2 fields above) so the hash ternary decides between <AppShell/> alone and the full <Header/><main/><Footer/> marketing tree, instead of nesting a swap inside a shared <main>. Header and Footer no longer render on any app-shell hash.

round1_advisories_carried_forward_unchan: AC-2: prop-types dependency exception — approved, no action needed.
AC-3: internal nav not hash-addressable past the entry hash — accepted trade-off, no action needed now.
AC-4: Header's own nav linking to #master-data stops being a live conflict once AC-1's fix lands (Header doesn't render on app-shell hashes) — no action needed beyond AC-1.
open_items_for_architecture_critic: Re-verify AC-1's required_fix is correctly reflected in app_jsx_change (round 2) and routing_design.app_shell_owns_its_own_chrome before clearing this stage for stage 3.3.
